Boy do I not agree with this list.

1) Pandemic becomes a game of quarterbacking and memorization. A lot of times, whether or not you're going to win or lose is decided by the shuffle of the cards at the beginning of the game. Leacock has made better co-op games.

2) Arkham Horror: while hardcore ameri-trash gamers will love it, it takes hours to play, has a bunch of fiddy rules, and comes down to blind luck frequently. As someone who actually enjoys Arkham, I can't recommend to most players. If you like the theme, I recommend the Streamlined and improved Eldritch Horror.

3) Decent: Are we considering Group vs 1 games to be co-op? Isn't that a team game? Anyways, if we're going to count games that are run by a game master, than Star Wars Imperial Assault should be above Decent. It made so many improvements to the formula that regular Decent players have tried to incorporate them into Decent to improve it.

4) Battlestar Galactica: Another team game. 3 vs 2 does not make a co-op game. While I enjoy Battlestar, it is near impossible to bring new players into the game. There are so many options each turn it feels impossible to know what to do. And because half of the players are working against you, it's impossible for them to help. God forbid if a new player ends up being the Cylon, get ready for the most boring 2 hours of your life. A better alternative is Dead of Winter, the options are simpler and new players know what they are suppose to do.

5) Space Alert: I won't get into that one again. In short, real time games try to solve the quarterbacking problem of co-op by making no one really interact with each other at all. I have no better alternative for this, because I hate real time games.

6) Friedrich: Never played it, but it's another 1 vs all game. So not really co-op.

7) Shadows over Camelot: another team game! This list should be called "best team games to play. I've never played it, but most people seem to think that it's a weaker version of Battlestar, without the simplicity of Dead of Winter.

8) Last Night On Earth: This is getting ridiculous. Another team game? I have no real complaints about this besides that it's pure ameritrash and uses roll-to-move. It's fun and stupid and will garner a lot of laughs from people. It runs a little long some times, but with the right group you're creating your own B-rated movie while playing. But once again, it's not a co-op.

9) Fury of Dracula: Never played, another team game. Next.

10) Ghost Stories: Holy shit. An actual co-op game. We haven't seen one of those since #2. However, I've never played it, so I can't say anything about it. It should be #3 though, since #3-9 aren't co-ops.

11) Werewofl: This guy isn't even trying. Besides being a party game that can be played with a deck of cards that has been remade into much better games; it's not a co-op. It's most vs some. If you're playing anyone other than the game, it's not co op.

To save time, I'm going to skip games I haven't played, since they become more obscure. However, I will point out that most of them are still not true co-op games.

17) Betrayal at House on the Hill: Not co-op. 1 vs many. My biggest gripe with this game is that you can barely even call it a team game. The first half of the game is everyone moving around with no real goal, and no real inclination to help each other. And then, randomly, the game changes, arbitrarily picks who's on who's teams and has a brand new batch of rules to read. People will defend the game saying that it creates a new story each time. But I personally get annoyed at having to read whole new rules in the middle of a game.

31) Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: a real co-op game. Really good, recommend it if you like racking your brain and think you can do what Holmes does.

61) Forbidden Island: How this is so low on the list with Pandemic being #1 is a mystery to me. It's a stream-lined, lighter version of Pandemic with less upkeep. It plays quick, is intense, and unlike most games on this list is an actual co-op. It suffers from quarterbacking, but being a 20 minute game, it's less annoying.

67) Castle Panic: Apparently he was hiding all of the real co-ops at the bottom of the list. While enjoyable, the game is just too easy without the expansion. Quarterbacking as usual, but the game state changes so quickly, it's usually a conversation.

68) Flashpoint: Be a firefighter! Pretty fun game, solves the problem of Pandemic with dice. You literally have no idea where the fire is going to spread. Completely random. Feels like a real fire. However, the randomness can sometimes dick you over pretty hard.

Overall, I'm not impressed with this list. More than half of it isn't co-op, and the games that are co-op have better alternatives.

Edit: Note: I noticed that the author of this geek list stopped at #36. Anything after that was added by other users.
